record.paper_title: The Critical Beta-splitting Random Tree II: Overview and Open Problems
record.original_question: For the standard cladogram drawing of DTCS(n), study the drawn width profile W(h), where W(h) counts the number of vertical lines crossing the strip (h,h+1), equivalently the number of clades whose draw-height is at most h and that arise from a split of a clade whose draw-height is at least h+1.

evidence.quote: Open Problem 15 What can we say about the drawn width profile process (W(h), h ≥ 0) for DTCS(n), for the number W(h) of vertical lines that cross an interval (h, h + 1), that is the number of clades with height ≤ h that arise as a split of a clade with height ≥ h + 1?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the discrete-time critical beta-splitting random tree on $n$ leaves, denoted $\mathrm{DTCS}(n)$, defined recursively as follows. Start with the set $[n]=\{1,2,\dots,n\}$ at the root. At each internal node labelled by a set $S$ with $|S|=m\ge 2$, choose a split size $i\in\{1,2,\dots,m-1\}$ with probability
$$q(m,i)=\frac{1}{Z_m}\cdot\frac{1}{i(m-i)},\qquad Z_m=\sum_{j=1}^{m-1}\frac{1}{j(m-j)},$$
partition $S$ uniformly at random into a subset of size $i$ (the "left child clade") and a subset of size $m-i$ (the "right child clade"), and recurse independently on each child. The recursion terminates at singletons (leaves).

A "clade" is the leaf-set associated with any node of the tree. Draw $\mathrm{DTCS}(n)$ as a standard cladogram in the plane as follows. Each clade $C$ is drawn as a horizontal line segment at integer height equal to its draw-height, defined recursively by: a singleton clade has draw-height $0$, and a clade arising as the parent of two child clades has draw-height $1+\max(h_L,h_R)$, where $h_L,h_R$ are the draw-heights of its two children. Each internal node (split) is drawn so that the parent clade's horizontal segment connects to its two children's segments by vertical line segments running between the parent's height and each child's height.

For an integer $h\ge 0$, define the drawn width profile
$$W(h)=\#\{\text{vertical line segments of the cladogram that cross the horizontal strip } \mathbb{R}\times(h,h+1)\},$$
equivalently the number of clades $C$ of $\mathrm{DTCS}(n)$ such that the draw-height of $C$ is at most $h$ while the draw-height of the parent clade of $C$ is at least $h+1$.

Study the process $(W(h):h\ge 0)$. In particular, determine its asymptotic distributional behavior as $n\to\infty$ (after any necessary rescaling of $h$ and of $W$), describe its mean, fluctuations, and any scaling limit as a stochastic process in $h$.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is stated as an open problem in the 2023 survey on the critical beta-splitting random tree, and subsequent works (e.g., the 2024 paper on the exchangeable partition representation and fringe tree, and the 2024 contraction-method paper) develop related aspects but do not address the drawn width profile process W(h). No published resolution was located.

status_evidence.title: The Critical Beta-splitting Random Tree II: Overview and Open Problems
status_evidence.snippet: Lists Open Problem 15 on the drawn width profile process (W(h), h ≥ 0) for DTCS(n).
status_evidence.claim: The drawn width profile is explicitly posed as an open problem.

status_evidence.title: The Critical Beta-splitting Random Tree III
status_evidence.snippet: Develops the exchangeable partition representation and fringe tree, without resolving the drawn width profile.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent work focuses on other aspects of the model.

status_evidence.title: Critical beta-splitting, via contraction
status_evidence.snippet: Uses contraction methods for heights and related statistics in the critical beta-splitting tree.
status_evidence.claim: Related but does not analyze the drawn width profile.
